**Course Description**  
**Faculty of Shari’ah**  
**PHD in the Islamic Creed**

---

**0431933 Islamic Philosophy** (3 credit hours)  
This course deals with the origins of modern philosophy and how to leakage of Islamic thought and the flags of Muslim philosophers, and their beliefs affiliations and beliefs.

---

**0401937 Creed of General Muslims (1)** (3 credit hours)  
This course deals with an in-depth study of the Qur’anic and Prophetic approach to creed matters, the method by which the Companions received the Qur'an and the Sunnah and the methodology they eventually adopted then the way by which the followers and their followers dealt with creed matters until the rise of groups that discussed the subject of creed and the methodology the scholars adopted in answering these groups and confirming the creed.

---

**0401938 Creed of General Muslims (2)** (3 credit hours)  
This course deals with an in-depth study of the reasons that lied behind the rise of the Ash’ari and Maturidi schools, the most significant creed matters they dealt with, the reasons for the emergence of this method and their efforts in writing back to the Mu’tazilites, the disbelievers and other groups. What is more, the course deals with the most distinguished scholars in the two schools in the past and present.

---

**0401939 Studies in Islamic Sects** (3 credit hours)  
This course deals with a detailed study of Hadith of separation, the internal and external sects reasons for the rise of the factors behind the survival of some and the extinction of others. The course also studies the most distinguished issues, into which the groups went, such as Imamate, Attakfir, Ataw'il, Assifat and Al-Ma’ad. The course also deals with the groups of Al-Kawarij, Ash’ari, Al-Murji’ah, Al-Kadareah, Al-Jabreh, Al-Mu’tazilah (Al-Jahmiah), Al-Mushabbisihah and Al-Mu’tazilah.

---

**0401940 Issues in Theological Rhetoric (Kalam)** (3 credit hours)  
This course deals with the definition of theological rhetoric, the factors behind its rise, the phases of its development, its legal ruling, the scholar's position towards it in the past and present, and clarifies the need for it.

---
